regions.name: Tequila Valley (Valle de Tequila), Jalisco
regions.geography: Low valley around the town of Tequila; volcanic soils, warmer and drier than the highlands.
regions.distinctions: Agave grows smaller and more herbaceous than highland agave; valley blancos read savory and vegetal in editorial guidance — a cultural description, not a legal boundary.

regions.name: Jalisco highlands (Los Altos / La Alteña), Jalisco
regions.geography: High plateau east of the valley (around Arandas and the La Alteña area); red mineral soils, cooler nights.
regions.distinctions: Highland agave reads sweeter and more floral in editorial guidance; some traditionalists stone-roast. A cultural/agronomic distinction, not a legal class.

regions.name: Valles Centrales, Oaxaca
regions.geography: Valley system around Oaxaca City, including Santiago Matatlán and Tlacolula.
regions.distinctions: Heartland of palenque mezcal; pechuga is a specific distillation tradition here, not a category of its own.

regions.name: Sierra Norte, Oaxaca
regions.geography: High mountains north of the valleys; high-altitude wild agave country.
regions.distinctions: Tobalá grows here and beyond; finding a mature tobalá is a matter of personal pride for a mezcalero — a cultural note, not a legal area.

regions.name: Sierra de Sonora (mountain country), Sonora
regions.geography: Mountain municipalities (Aconchi, Álamos, San Pedro de la Cueva, and neighbors) where bacanora vinatas work.
regions.distinctions: Bacanora's official coverage is municipal within Sonora (since the 2000 DO), never the whole state.

regions.name: Sierra Occidental de Jalisco
regions.geography: Mountain country west of Guadalajara, around La Vieja and the Sierra de Talpa.
regions.distinctions: Sierra raicilla taberna country; the DO declaration names specific municipalities in Jalisco, so no whole-state shading.

regions.name: Costa Sur / Cabo Corrientes, Jalisco
regions.geography: Coastal mountains and canyons of southwestern Jalisco, around Cabo Corrientes.
regions.distinctions: Costa is an editorial tradition split of raicilla, not a legal class.

regions.name: Tuxcacuesco region, southern Jalisco (Jalisco–Colima borderlands)
regions.geography: Southern Jalisco river canyons around Tuxcacuesco and Zapotitlán de Vadillo, reaching across the state line into northern Colima — the Río Almería valley and the volcano's lower slopes.
regions.distinctions: Tuxca has no denomination of origin; vinatero practice is cultural, and bottles carry no NOM registration — the absence is of DO-scheme certification, not of other labeling obligations — a legal fact, not an authenticity judgment. The tradition is borderlands: it reaches into northern Colima, but the app's cited example is a Jalisco-made bottle, which does not by itself establish Colima production coverage.

regions.name: Comitán de Domínguez, Chiapas
regions.geography: Highland plateau of central Chiapas around Comitán de Domínguez.
regions.distinctions: Comiteco is protected since October 2025 as the Indicación Geográfica “Comiteco de Comitán, Chiapas” (an IG, not a DO); composition (agave vs cane sugars) is verified per bottle, never assumed.

regions.name: Nanacamilpa and central Tlaxcala
regions.geography: Pulque heartland on the Tlaxcala–State of México highlands.
regions.distinctions: Destilado de pulque is a regional tradition, explicitly not mezcal; fermented pulque itself is not a spirit and stays out of the catalogue.

regions.name: Northern Chihuahuan Sierra, Chihuahua
regions.geography: Sierra and desert country of northern Chihuahua, from the Sierra to Delicias.
regions.distinctions: Sotol's DO (2002) covers Chihuahua, Coahuila and Durango; Dasylirion is not an agave, and the app keeps that explicit.

regions.name: La Montaña (mountain Guerrero)
regions.geography: Mountain municipalities of eastern Guerrero, in the Balsas basin — Apango and neighboring communities where papalote mezcal is made.
regions.distinctions: App coverage, not a legal boundary: Guerrero is a major mezcal state under the DO, and papalote here names a cupreata-lineage agave of these mountains; local names need their geographic context.

regions.name: Sierra El Mezquital, Durango
regions.geography: High sierra of El Mezquital municipality, Durango — pine country where Tepehuán vinateros work cenizo at elevation.
regions.distinctions: App coverage, not a legal boundary: Durango lies within the mezcal DO, and a vinata — not a palenque — is the Durango word for a small distillery.

regions.name: Altiplano Potosino (central plateau), San Luis Potosí
regions.geography: Rocky, arid central Potosino plateau around Santa Isabel and neighboring communities — the home of maguey verde (Agave salmiana) mezcal.
regions.distinctions: App coverage, not a legal boundary: the salmiana here is the plateau's wild maguey verde, cooked mezcal-style — a different tradition from the pulquero sap harvest of the same species farther south.

regions.name: Rio de Parras, Michoacán
regions.geography: River-valley communities of the Trans-Mexican Volcanic Belt in Michoacán — Rio de Parras and neighboring vinata country where cupreata (penca ancha) mezcal is made.
regions.distinctions: App coverage, not a legal boundary: Michoacán is a major mezcal state under the DO, and penca ancha is the Rio de Parras name for a cupreata-lineage agave; local names need their geographic context.

regions.name: Mixteca Poblana, Puebla
regions.geography: Hills of the Mixteca Poblana around San Diego La Mesa Tochimilitzingo and neighboring communities — papalometl mezcal country.
regions.distinctions: App coverage, not a legal boundary: Puebla is a major mezcal state under the DO, and papalometl here names Agave potatorum in the bottle's documented case — the same word can name other agaves elsewhere, so local names need their geographic context.
